stories.title: Set up a teammate
stories.premise: The human asks for a job; the agent asks for a cap.
stories.statusNote: Four drawings, no live issuer route: the screens are rendered from the same layout modules that draw the pass, and the setup route they depict is not in the app.
stories.notThis: Not a working issuer flow: these four screens are drawings, and the setup route they show is not built.

frames.title: Pick the job
frames.alt: An iPhone screenshot of paystage.xyz/new in Safari: four job presets with their limits, and a step bar reading 1 Pick.
frames.caption: Safari, on the phone. Four presets, each already carrying a limit. Picking one only opens the next screen — nothing is issued here, and no prompt appears.

frames.title: Configure the numbers
frames.alt: An iPhone screenshot of the configure screen in Safari with editable fields for per purchase, per day, expiry and payees.
frames.caption: Still Safari. Every number is editable, which is the difference between a preset and a policy: the human changes what they mean, not what we chose.

frames.title: Confirm, then Face ID
frames.alt: An iPhone screenshot with a read-back of the limits and an iOS Face ID sheet asking to confirm.
frames.caption: The read-back comes first: what is being granted, in numbers, before any biometric. Only then does iOS draw its own sheet with the Face ID glyph. We choose when it appears; we never draw it.
frames.correction: A person does not pick one of four options and have Face ID fire. Pick, configure, read back, confirm — four steps, and the prompt is the fourth.

frames.title: Safari hands it to Wallet
frames.alt: An iPhone screenshot in Safari offering Add to Apple Wallet for a signed Vouch pass.
frames.caption: The pass is signed and handed to the Wallet app. After this screen the page holds nothing — the wallet does. This is a transition between two apps, and it is the step people miss.
frames.correction: The page cannot show the pass after this point. If the hand-off fails, nothing is provisioned and the serial has no pass to revoke.

stories.title: The teammate works
stories.premise: Forty payments happen and the human sees none of them.
stories.statusNote: Three drawings of a fixture. The product's API produces verdicts, but no endpoint produced this table, and no screen here is a live dashboard.
stories.notThis: Not a dashboard you can open: the list is a fixture, and every number on it is invented for the drawing.

frames.title: The work nobody watches
frames.surface: the agent's log, not a screen
frames.alt: A list of payments with times, payees, amounts and verdicts, headed 40 payments today and notifications sent: 0.
frames.caption: This list is the whole user-visible surface of an agent spending money. The human sees it when they go looking, which is the design and not an outage.
frames.correction: Every value here is a fixture. No endpoint produced this table, and the page would rather say so than let a screenshot imply a workload that does not exist yet.

frames.title: A refusal at the cap
frames.surface: the agent's verdict, not a screen
frames.alt: A do_not_pay verdict naming the per-payment cap, the payee, and that no signature was produced.
frames.caption: The agent receives the rule that fired and the numbers, then stops. A refusal that says only "outside policy" is a support ticket, not an answer.

frames.title: A review arriving
frames.surface: the agent's verdict, not a screen
frames.alt: A review verdict carrying the amount, its share of the allowance, the checks run and the checks skipped.
frames.caption: The middle verdict: not a yes, not a no. It carries what was checked and — the part nobody else prints — what was not, including whether the seller delivers.

stories.title: The human adjusts
stories.premise: The limit is too low. The agent asks; the human taps.
stories.statusNote: Two drawings. The live /m/:serial page is read-only; the change controls in the first drawing are not built, so there is no manage page to link.
stories.notThis: Not a manage page: the live record page is read-only, so there is nothing here to click that changes a limit.
stories.linkNote: No live link: there is no manage page. The live /m/:serial page is read-only and offers no control that could change a limit.

frames.title: The page would be the editor
frames.alt: The mandate page drawing: the same tint, mark and teammate name as the pass, with the limits and change controls.
frames.caption: Same tint, same mark, same name as the pass in the wallet — in this drawing the page is the pass with controls on it. The agent drafts every change; the human is the only one who can approve one. AP2 has a word for this screen: a Trusted Surface, a non-agentic interface that renders the mandate to the human.
frames.correction: The live /m/:serial page is read-only. The change… and remove controls in this drawing are not built, and the live page says so instead of offering a control that cannot work.

frames.title: The pass would update
frames.alt: The same pass after a change, with the new limits on the face.
frames.caption: One tap, and the wallet pass shows the new numbers. There is no second card to keep in sync.
frames.correction: Nothing writes a changed pass today: this is the second half of the same drawing, not a screen the product can reach.

stories.title: The human stops
stories.premise: One action, and the name comes off.
stories.statusNote: Three drawings. Revocation is modelled as a separate signed statement; the revoke screen here is a drawing, and the live record page has no revoke control.
stories.notThis: Not a revoke button: the screen is a drawing, and the live record page cannot stop a pass.

frames.title: One action
frames.alt: A page with one primary action: Stop this pass.
frames.caption: Revocation is a signed statement, not an edit: the pass is immutable, so stopping it is a second object that names the serial. A revocation that needs re-signing is one that gets lost in a queue.
frames.correction: The live /m/:serial page has no revoke control. This drawing shows the action a client would send, not a button shipped on the record page.

frames.title: The face says so
frames.alt: The same pass in grey with a REVOKED state, all colour removed.
frames.caption: The pass keeps its place in the wallet and loses its colour and its claim. Nothing is deleted, so nothing can be quietly restored.

frames.title: Deleting the pass is not revoking it
frames.alt: A diagram comparing removing the pass from the wallet with revoking it.
frames.caption: The misunderstanding worth a frame: removing the image from a phone changes nothing on the server. Only revocation changes what the endpoint says to a stranger.

stories.title: A stranger checks
stories.premise: Someone has never heard of us and wants one answer.
stories.statusNote: One drawing and one live page. /verify answers active, revoked, expired or unknown today; the four-card stack is a drawing.
stories.notThis: Not a gallery of real passes: the four cards are a drawing, and /verify only answers the serial you give it.

frames.title: Four teammates, one principal
frames.alt: Four passes fanned like cards, each a different tint with its own teammate name and cap.
frames.caption: Each teammate gets its own cap and its own tint, and revoking one leaves the others alone.
frames.correction: The caps are set by hand, one at a time. The agent may draft a change, but it cannot add a teammate or raise a cap.

frames.title: The scan page — live
frames.surface: the live page, not a drawing
frames.caption: A stranger scans the QR and lands on one page with one answer: active, revoked, expired or unknown. That page is /verify, and the link below is the page itself rather than a picture of it.
frames.correction: No image on purpose: a screenshot of /verify would go stale, and the live page is one click away.

stories.title: Something goes wrong
stories.premise: The cases nobody puts in a demo.
stories.statusNote: Four drawings of failure states. Two further drawings (unknown serial, cap mid-job) are not shown, because a story carries at most four frames.
stories.notThis: Not a live incident feed: the failures are drawings of the state machine, not screenshots of an outage.

frames.title: Our service is down
frames.alt: A three-step diagram: the agent asks for a verdict, the adapter refuses, no signature is produced.
frames.caption: Fail closed, by design: an unreachable gate is not an approval. The alternative turns every outage into an unguarded spending window.

frames.title: Face ID cancelled
frames.alt: A diagram: the biometric prompt is cancelled, so no mandate exists to spend.
frames.caption: Nothing is issued, so there is nothing to spend and nothing to revoke. The agent learns why and stops.

frames.title: A stale image, a live answer
frames.alt: A diagram comparing a screenshot that says active with a live endpoint that answers revoked.
frames.caption: The QR is the authority, not the picture. An old image is a claim about the past — which is also why a pass cannot be verified offline.

frames.title: The free allowance runs out
frames.surface: an API response, not a screen
frames.alt: A 429 body saying the free tier is exhausted, that the service is working, and where the paid path is.
frames.caption: A caller must be able to tell "capped" from "broken". The body names the cap, says the service is working, and gives the reset.
